t: Personal AI OS: what actually makes AI smarter
s: Not more skills: good memory (organized Markdown), a few sharp skills, real tools (search, code, files) and verification. Skills teach how; MCP connects tools; memory gives context.
x: Order: memory → 3 skills → shared workspace → tools → automation + review.
Skills load only when relevant, so a few precise ones beat many overlapping ones.

s: A skill is a folder with SKILL.md: a name, a description that says when to use it, and instructions. Claude loads it only when the task matches the description.
x: Source check: PRIMARY.
Write the description as triggers: 'Use when I…'.
Keep one skill per recurring workflow.

s: CLAUDE.md files load automatically at session start: project rules, preferences, key facts. Keep them short and point to other files for detail.

t: Second brain method: CODE + PARA (Tiago Forte)
s: CODE = Capture (save what resonates, don't over-filter), Organize, Distill (pull out the key points over time), Express (turn notes into output). PARA files by actionability: Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives.
x: Source check: SECONDARY (not yet verified against a primary source).
The goal is output (projects, content), not a pretty archive.
Organize by project, not by topic: 'where will I use this?'

s: One idea per note, titled as a claim, densely linked to other notes, rewritten over time. Links beat folders: an atomic note can be reused by every topic it touches.
x: Source check: PRIMARY.
Built on Niklas Luhmann's Zettelkasten.
Write notes for yourself; refine them each time you revisit.

s: Workflows: AI + tools follow fixed code paths. Agents: the model decides its own steps and tool use. Start with the simplest solution; agents trade cost and speed for flexibility.
x: Source check: PRIMARY.
Successful teams use simple, composable patterns, not heavy frameworks.
Predictable steps → workflow (like my systems/). Open-ended tasks → agent.

s: What the AI sees matters more than clever prompts. Context is a limited attention budget: more text can lower accuracy ('context rot'). Keep instructions small, tools few and clear, and load details just in time.
x: Source check: PRIMARY.
Claude Code pattern: CLAUDE.md up front, files searched on demand (grep/glob).
Long tasks: compaction, structured notes, sub-agents.

s: 'LLM as an operating system': core memory always in context, recall memory (past conversations, searchable), archival memory (long-term, searchable). The agent edits its own memory and consolidates it while idle.
x: Source check: SECONDARY (not yet verified against a primary source).
Paper: 'MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems' (UC Berkeley, 2023); now Letta, open source.
Memory degrades without pruning and consolidation.

t: How my AI OS maps to the research
s: Core memory = CLAUDE.md + memory/CONTEXT.md. Recall = brain/log.md. Archival = Second Brain stars + Drive vault. Workflows = systems/. Consolidation = Daily optimizer. Gap: app notes don't reach Claude's memory yet.

t: Finfluencer rules (EU + Belgium): educate, don't advise
s: Explaining how investing works is allowed. Telling followers what to buy/sell, especially tailored to them, can be investment advice, which in Belgium needs FSMA authorization. EU market-abuse rules: say who you are, be objective, disclose conflicts (holdings, partners). Paid posts must be labeled.
x: Source check: PRIMARY (Wikifin, the FSMA's financial-education site).
Investedia guardrails: education + examples, no 'buy X' calls, disclose own positions and sponsors, add 'not financial advice / for education'.
Never promote unauthorized platforms or products: can make you complicit in fraud.
Not legal advice: check FSMA's own guidance before monetizing.

t: ESMA: investment recommendations on social media
s: ESMA and national supervisors state that anyone recommending investments on social media falls under the Market Abuse Regulation: identify yourself, present recommendations objectively, disclose interests. Breaches can mean fines or referral to prosecutors.
x: Source check: SECONDARY (ESMA statement as republished by a national regulator; see the Belgium factsheet for the primary source).
Verified: ESMA published national finfluencer factsheets in Jan 2026, including one for Belgium (see 'Belgium finfluencer factsheet').

t: Instagram Reels: watch time, likes and sends per reach
s: Instagram's own explanation (May 2023): Reels are ranked mainly by your activity (what you liked, saved, reshared, commented on), your history with the creator, information about the reel (audio, visuals, popularity) and about the creator. Instagram's head Adam Mosseri later reportedly stressed watch time, likes per reach and sends per reach.
x: Source check: PRIMARY for the official list (about.instagram.com); Mosseri's 3 signals SECONDARY.
For Investedia: content people save and reshare, strong opening for watch time.

s: Market-data/education sites: TradingView (~209M visits/mo), Finviz (~17.8M), Stock Analysis (~8.4M, built by one founder since 2019). Winners own one clear promise or tool, rank a page per ticker/term in Google, and grow a free newsletter.

s: The big sites cover everything; winners own one clear promise. Candidate: markets explained for young Europeans, one chart and one sentence.
A page per stock or term that answers one question in plain language. Stock Analysis gets most traffic from ticker searches.
'3 market moves explained in 60 seconds'. An email list is an audience you own; Market Bullets reportedly reached ~168k readers.
One concept per video, strong first 2 seconds, a reason to send it to a friend. Top of funnel to the site.

t: The first 2 seconds decide a Reel
s: Watch time is the strongest Reels signal, so the opening must earn the next second: a surprising number, a question, or a visible result.

t: Sends bring new people, likes keep followers
s: Likes per reach mostly helps reach among followers; DM sends help reach non-followers. Write content people want to forward.
Sending only the most relevant notes saves tokens and can improve accuracy ('context rot'). Small instructions, few clear tools.
Notes and AI memory degrade without merging duplicates, pruning stale items and adding links. The weekly review does this.
Atomic, linked notes can be reused by every topic they touch, which makes the galaxy smarter than long mixed notes.
tests/smoke.js opens the app at phone and desktop size with a fake AI and checks errors, panels, Ask, data integrity and edits. Runs on GitHub every push and nightly; costs no AI tokens.
Edit only app/index.html; tools/build-claude-page.py builds the Claude page from it, so changes aren't made twice.
Research saved in app/knowledge.json appears as stars on every device; Ask and Talk use it.
Repeatable check of competitors: same-source traffic estimates, features, formats, 1-3 ranked actions. Say 'check competitors'.

You stay responsible for what you post; misleading or reckless messages can create legal liability. Disclose any payment, gift or benefit openly (not just a hashtag). Statements must be true, fair, clear and not misleading, with facts separated from opinions.

High-risk products often pushed by finfluencers: CFDs, forex, futures, some crowdfunding, volatile crypto: you can lose 100%.
Investedia: label opinions as opinions, show sources for facts, never promote these products.

s: Testing yourself at growing intervals (1, 3, 7, 21 days) beats cramming or rereading. A meta-analysis of 29 studies found a large benefit (g = 0.74); effects are smaller in some subjects (math g = 0.28).

t: Programmatic SEO vs Google's scaled content abuse
s: Google's spam policy (updated 2026-08-28): scaled content abuse = 'many pages generated for the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings and not helping users', 'no matter how it's created'. Examples: AI-generated pages without added value, scraped/stitched content, pages that make little sense but contain keywords.
x: Source check: PRIMARY (Google Search Central).
Investedia: template pages are allowed only if each adds real value for users (own explanation, context), not just keywords.

s: beehiiv (official pricing): free up to 2,500 subscribers, 0% of paid subscription revenue (Stripe fees apply), but the referral program needs a paid plan (Lite, from $49/mo billed annually). Substack: free to start; takes 10% of paid subscriptions (widely reported; its help page blocked our check).
x: Source check: PRIMARY for beehiiv (pricing page); SECONDARY for Substack's 10%.
Start free on either; referrals cost money on beehiiv.

t: Market data: delayed data is free to use, distributing may cost
s: Euronext must offer 15-minute-delayed data free of charge (MiFID II art. 13). Its terms: use is free 'except in the event of distribution', where fees and Subscriber Terms may apply. Showing prices on a public site counts as distribution. Real-time data is always fee-liable.
x: Source check: PRIMARY (Euronext delayed-data terms).
Investedia: before showing prices publicly, check your data provider's display/redistribution terms, or use charts/widgets from a provider that licenses public display.
Investedia today uses Yahoo's unofficial endpoint; Yahoo's terms forbid automated collection and redistribution. Safer: TradingView widgets (free, branded, delayed stocks).

t: Affiliate links on a finance site
s: Common model: clear disclosure ('I may earn a commission, at no cost to you') and marking which partners you actually reviewed. Broker affiliates can fall under the broker's regulator rules.
x: Source check: SECONDARY/adjacent.
Belgium: FSMA treats referral exemptions narrowly (insurance guidance); for investment broker affiliates, ask FSMA or a lawyer first.
Belgian factsheet: disclose any benefit openly.

t: Investing in ETFs from Belgium: taxes
s: Stock-exchange tax (TOB), per buy and per sell, 3 rates with caps (broker tariff Jan 2026): 0.12% (max 1,300 euro), 0.35% (max 1,600 euro), 1.32% (max 4,000 euro, Belgian-registered accumulating funds). Most Irish/Luxembourg ETFs not registered in Belgium: 0.12%. Dividends: 30% withholding (first ~833 euro exempt in 2026).
x: Source check: SECONDARY (broker tariff + Curvo); official fin.belgium.be page blocked our check.
Check your broker's applied rate before buying.

s: Define specific, measurable success criteria, then test with many realistic cases and automated grading (code, model or human graders). More slightly-noisier automated tests beat a few hand-graded ones.

t: Agents in practice: start with a workflow
s: Use a fixed workflow when steps are predictable; use an agent only when the task is open-ended and the tools are trusted. Agents cost more and are slower; add them when a workflow clearly fails.
x: My setup follows this: systems/ = workflows, Claude Code sessions = agent.

t: Deliberate practice matters, but quality matters most
s: Macnamara 2014 (88 studies): practice explained 26% of performance in games, 21% music, 18% sports, 4% education. Reanalyses find much more when practice is individualized and high-quality.
x: Source check: PRIMARY (abstract, Psychological Science 2014).
Critiques: reanalyses with stricter criteria find more variance explained; quality and individualization matter.
For me: focused practice on weak spots with fast feedback, not just hours.

s: Prompting learners to explain material in their own words gives a small-to-moderate learning boost (Bisra 2018 meta-analysis); preparing to teach also helps (protégé effect). The Feynman technique builds on this, though it has no direct studies.

Use Talk: explain a topic back to Claude in plain words; gaps show what to relearn.

t: Free market data for a public site: the real rules
s: TradingView widgets: free with branding, but its Terms of Use forbid commercial use without a separate agreement. CoinGecko Demo: 10k calls/month, attribution required, commercial terms unclear. FRED: allowed with a 'not endorsed by the St. Louis Fed' notice. Twelve Data free: internal non-display only. No free source clearly allows public display on a commercial site.
x: Source check: PRIMARY (official terms and pricing, checked 2026-10-17).
Monetized site → budget for a licence that includes public display.

t: Republishing news: headlines + links are the safe part
s: The EU press publishers' right (Directive 2019/790, art. 15) does not cover hyperlinks or 'individual words or very short extracts'. Longer snippets can need a licence; 'very short' isn't defined. Yahoo's terms forbid commercial redistribution of its content.
x: Source check: SECONDARY for the article wording (EUR-Lex blocked automated access); PRIMARY for Yahoo terms.
Investedia: keep headline + source + link; keep descriptions very short or drop them.
